questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. To think that a computer would one day replace a book is indeed unthinkable and far fetched.

B. The thoughts and ideas contained in a book are immortal like Tulsidas’ Ram Charitra Manas, Ved Vyas’ Mahabharata, The Bible and many other religious and literary works like Shakespeare’s plays etc.

C. On the other hand a computer is but a machine, that at best can visually display the contents of a specific book.

D. A good book in the words of John Milton “is the precious lifeblood of a master spirit, embalmed and treasured up to a purpose to a life beyond life."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'DBCA'.**

• Sentence **C **would come next as this sentence is comparing computers with books.
 
• Sentence **A **would be the last sentence as it concludes the comparison between book and computer.

Hence, the correct answer is **'DBCA'.**

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hale and hearty
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Strong and healthy'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The meaning of the idiom **'Hale and hearty'** is **'Strong and healthy'.**

 
 
• **E.g.**__- She is still **hale and hearty** in her nineties.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is **'Strong and healthy'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• The term **'hale and hearty'** derives from Old English, the language spoken in England prior to the late 11th century. In Old English, the word **'hal'** means **'safe'** or **'unhurt'**. It is the root word of the modern English words '**whole'** and '**heal'** as well as **'health'** and '**hail'**. The modern English word '**hale'** meaning **fit and healthy**, derives from this root.
 
• The word '**hearty'** first appears in the 14th century and is used to mean '**spirited'** or '**courageous'**. In the Middle Ages, the heart was thought to be the seat of feelings. As a result, a wide variety of English terms refer to the heart in this way. Examples include '**hard-hearted'**, **heartfelt'** and '**heartbreak'**. To be '**hearty'**, therefore, is **to have a strong heart and to be in high spirits.**

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Fiona enquired whether I had gone to school on Tuesday

options.text: “Had you been going to school on Tuesday?” Fiona asked me.
“Where are you going on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me.
“Did you go to school on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me.
“Are you gone to school on Tuesday? Fiona enquired.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **“Did you go to school on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me****.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is enquiring about something. So, the Direct Speech of this sentence must be an interrogative sentence.
 
• The rule of changing an indirect speech into a direct speech of an Interrogative sentence is as follows:
 
 
• In Indirect Narration, interrogative Verbs such as **“ask”, “enquire”, “demand”, “want to know”** etc are used as Reporting Verbs before the Reported Speech in place of simple Verb **“say” or “tell”**.
 
• **E.g.**__- He said to me, "Are you ill?" **(Direct Speech)**
 
• He **asked** (or **enquired of**) me if (or whether) I was ill. **(Indirect Speech)**
 
• If the Reported Speech in Direct Narration is introduced by Verbs like **“ be”, “have”, “do”, or any other auxiliary Verbs like “can”, “shall”, “will”**, the connective **“ if ”, “ whether ”** is used after the Reporting Verb or object of the Reporting verb in the Indirect Narration.
 
• __**E.g.**__- He said to me, "Are you ill?" **(Direct Speech)**
 
• He asked (or enquired of) me **if** (or **whether**) I was ill. **(Indirect Speech)**** **
 
 

 Hence, the correct answer is **“Did you go to school on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **What is Direct & Indirect Speech?**

 
 
• **Direct speech** – reporting the message of the speaker in the exact words as spoken by him.
 
• **Direct speech example:** Maya said, "I am busy now."
 
• **Indirect speech **– reporting the message of the speaker in our own words.
 
• **Indirect speech example:** Maya said that she was busy then.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He didn’t / called me / in the / last week
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **called me**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The base form of verb **(V1) **is always used after 'do' and 'did'.

 
 
• For example:
 
 
• I did **go** there.
 
• I did not** know** about this secret place.
 
 
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, 'didn't' must be followed by the base form of verb.
 
• Hence, 'called' (V2) must be replaced by 'call' (V1).

Therefore, the correct answer is: *He didn’t **call **me in the last week.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

He invited me to his place yesterday.

options.text: I invited to his place yesterday.
I was invited by him to his place yesterday.
To his place I was invited yesterday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'I was invited by him to his place yesterday'.**

__
 
• The given sentence is in** Active Voice**. As per the question we have to change it into** Passive Voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject +V2 + Object. **(Active Voice)**
 
• Subject(objective case) + was/were +V3 + by + Object(subjective case)**. (Passive Voice)**
 
 
 
• **The subject** of the given sentence is **'he'.**
 
• **The object** of the given sentence is** 'me'.**
 
• **The subject** will be put in place of **the object** and **the object **will be put in place of** the subject.**

**Correct sentence:**__ I was invited by him to his place yesterday.
